answers.answer: For 2 players, each gets 4 starting Player cards; for 3, each gets 3; for 4, each gets 2. Remove Epidemic cards and set them aside before shuffling and dealing the remaining City and Event cards. Each player's matching pawn starts in Atlanta.
answers.evidence: Setup: remove Epidemic cards and deal 4/3/2 cards; place matching colored pawns in Atlanta.

answers.answer: Put the Infection Rate marker on the leftmost 2. Flip 3 Infection cards and put 3 matching cubes on each named city; flip 3 more and put 2 cubes on each; flip 3 more and put 1 cube on each. Put all 9 revealed cards on the Infection Discard Pile; the remaining cards form the Infection Deck. The summary does not specify the order/orientation used to put those 9 cards into the discard pile.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 8: leftmost 2; groups of three receive 3, 2, then 1 cubes; all 9 go to Infection Discard Pile and remaining cards form Infection Deck.

answers.answer: Use 4 Epidemics for Introductory, 5 for Standard, or 6 for Heroic; remove unused Epidemic cards. Divide the remaining Player cards into that many face-down piles as equal in size as possible, shuffle one Epidemic into each pile face down, and stack the piles with smaller piles on the bottom. The summary does not specify a tie-break for equal-sized piles.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 7 lists difficulty counts and pile preparation; unused Epidemics are removed and smaller piles go on the bottom.

answers.answer: Take up to 4 actions; repetitions are allowed and you may stop early. Cards discarded to pay action costs go to the Player Discard Pile. Then draw 2 Player cards together, resolving Epidemics first and discarding or playing Events until within the 7-card limit; then infect cities by the current infection rate. After all three phases, play passes to the left.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Actions: up to 4 actions; repeat or stop; discards go to Player Discard Pile; draw 2, then infect; pass left.

answers.answer: Drive/Ferry moves to a city connected by a white line and has no card cost. Direct Flight discards the City card naming the destination. Charter Flight discards the City card matching the city you are in and moves to any city. Shuttle Flight moves from a city with a research station to any other city with a research station. The summary says white lines going off one board edge wrap to the other edge (Sydney and Los Angeles are an example), so such a wrapped connection can be used for Drive/Ferry. No card cost is stated for Shuttle Flight.
answers.evidence: Movement Actions table; Special Rules: Board wrapping; Player Reference costs.

answers.answer: Normally, discard the City card matching your current city, take a research station from the supply, and place it in your city. If all six are built, relocate one from anywhere on the board. If more than six stations are supplied, set extras aside during setup; the summary provides no rule for using box-supplied extras beyond the six-station limit.
answers.evidence: Build a Research Station action and Special Rules: only 6 exist, relocate one if all are placed; set extras aside during setup.

answers.answer: One Treat Disease action removes one cube of one chosen color. Because the diseases are cured, the general action rule says return all cubes of one cured color in the city instead. The action treats each different color separately, so clearing the other cured color and uncured color requires separate actions; the uncured color is removed one cube per action. Return removed cubes to the cube supply.
answers.evidence: Treat Disease: remove 1 chosen-color cube, or all cubes of that color if cured; treat each different color with a separate action; cubes return to supply.

answers.answer: At any research station, discard 5 City cards of the same disease color (4 for the Scientist) and move that disease's cure marker to its Cure Indicator. The station city need not match the disease color. Existing cubes remain; cured diseases can still receive cubes during infections and Epidemics until eradicated. If there are no cubes of that color anywhere on the board when cured, eradicate it immediately and flip the marker.
answers.evidence: Cure Procedure: any station; 5 same-color cards (4 Scientist); existing cubes remain; no cubes on board means immediate eradication and marker flip.

answers.answer: Normally, the card transferred must be the City card matching the city both players occupy. Either player may give that card to the other or take it from the other, and both players must agree. If the recipient exceeds 7 cards, they immediately discard or play an Event until at most 7.
answers.evidence: Share Knowledge action; Hand Limit applies immediately after receiving a card, including via Share Knowledge.

answers.answer: When sharing, the Researcher may give any City card from the Researcher's hand to a player in the same city, not only the matching card. It can happen on either player's turn. The exception does not allow another player to give the Researcher an arbitrary nonmatching card; the summary does not grant that direction of transfer.
answers.evidence: Researcher exception: any City card transfer is from Researcher to other player, in same city, on either player's turn; no arbitrary nonmatching cards may be given to Researcher.

answers.answer: After actions, draw 2 Player cards together. If fewer than 2 cards remain when you need to draw, the game ends and players lose; discards are not reshuffled.
answers.evidence: Drawing Player Cards: draw top 2 together; if fewer than 2 remain, game ends and players lose (do not reshuffle discards).

answers.answer: Resolve Increase, Infect, then Intensify. Increase the Infection Rate marker by one. For Infect, draw the bottom Infection card; for a non-eradicated disease place cubes in its named city to reach 3 of that color. With 2 already there, add 1 cube, then an outbreak occurs; the summary's outbreak rule advances the Outbreaks marker and spreads one cube to every connected city, with chain reactions as applicable. Discard the Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile. Intensify by reshuffling only that discard pile and placing it on top of the Infection Deck. The resolved Epidemic is removed from the game and no replacement is drawn. The summary does not state the specific city connections needed to enumerate an outbreak's spread.
answers.evidence: Epidemic steps; outbreak rules; no replacement rule.

answers.answer: After 0, 1, and 2 Epidemics: 2 Infection cards per turn; after 3 and 4: 3; after 5 and 6: 4. Thus the requested sequence is 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4.
answers.evidence: Infection Rate Track in Player Reference: Epidemics 0–6 maps to cards 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4.

answers.answer: Resolve all three steps of the first Epidemic, then all three steps of the second; Events may be played between them. After both drawn Epidemics have been resolved, enforce the hand limit: discard or play Events until at most 7 cards.
answers.evidence: Two Epidemics at once are resolved fully in sequence and Events may be played between; Hand Limit says resolve all Epidemics drawn, then enforce limit.

answers.answer: During normal Infect Cities, flip cards from the top of the Infection Deck, one at a time, equal to the current infection rate. For a non-eradicated disease, place 1 matching cube in the named city unless it already has 3 of that color, in which case place no fourth cube and cause an outbreak. This includes cured-but-not-eradicated diseases, which can still get new cubes. For an eradicated disease, place no cube. Discard each Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Infecting Cities: top of deck, rate number one at a time; eradicated gets no cube; 3 cubes triggers outbreak; each card discarded. Cure Procedure confirms cured disease still infects until eradication.

answers.answer: When a city with 3 cubes receives a would-be fourth cube, it triggers an outbreak. Advance the Outbreaks marker once for each outbreak; add one cube to each connected city. If a connected city already has 3 of that color, its chain-reaction outbreak happens after the current outbreak resolves. Do not add a cube back into a city that has already had an outbreak during this Infection card. Different colors have separate caps: a city can have up to 3 cubes of each color.
answers.evidence: Outbreaks steps 1–4: marker advances per outbreak, spread to connected cities, chain reaction afterward, skip cities already outbreaked; 3 per color.

answers.answer: No. Airlift cannot be played between drawing an Infection card and resolving it, so it cannot move the Quarantine Specialist in time to prevent that card's outbreak. After the card is resolved, an Event may be played before the next card. Any player may play Airlift, and the player who plays it decides its use; it costs no action. Played Events go to the Player Discard Pile. Moving another player's pawn requires that player's permission.
answers.evidence: Event rules: any player, any time, not between drawing and resolving a card; player chooses use; Events are not actions and go to Player Discard Pile. Airlift requires permission for another player's pawn.

answers.answer: As an action, the Contingency Planner takes one Event card from anywhere in the Player Discard Pile and stores it on the Role card. Storage limit is one and it does not count against the hand limit. When played, remove the stored Event from the game instead of discarding it.
answers.evidence: Contingency Planner role text.

answers.answer: As an action, the Dispatcher can either move any pawn to a city with another pawn, or move another player's pawn as if it were their own. Both options require the owner's agreement when moving another player's pawn. Direct/Charter Flight cards come from the Dispatcher's hand; for a Charter Flight, the card matches the moved pawn's departure city. When directing another pawn, the Dispatcher may move it but cannot make it Treat Disease or take another nonmovement action, and cannot use the Operations Expert's special move.
answers.evidence: Dispatcher role text.

answers.answer: Players win immediately when cures for all 4 diseases are discovered; eradication and an empty board are not required. The three losses are: the Outbreaks marker reaches the last space (8th outbreak); the supply lacks enough cubes of a needed color to place the required cubes during an Epidemic, outbreak, or infection (immediate loss); or a player cannot draw 2 Player cards after their actions.
answers.evidence: Victory and Defeat sections; Cube supply check says immediate loss during epidemic, outbreak, or infection.

answers.answer: Place the board within reach and put the six research stations and separated disease cubes nearby; place one station in Atlanta; put the Outbreaks marker on 0 and the four Cure markers vial-side up near the Cure Indicators. Give each player a Reference card, shuffle Role cards, deal one face up to each, put matching pawns in Atlanta, and remove unused roles and pawns. The player with the highest-population City card goes first. Setup does not state a further special board-supply arrangement.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–5 and 9.

answers.answer: Teammates may offer advice, but the player whose turn it is decides their actions. Introductory hands are face up for everyone; Standard/Heroic hands are private by default, though experienced groups may choose open hands. Anyone may inspect either discard pile at any time.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; Special Rules: Introductory/Standard/Heroic hand visibility and discard-pile inspection.

answers.answer: Removing the last cube of an uncured disease does not eradicate it and has no effect. Removing the last cube of a cured disease eradicates it; flip its cure marker to the eradication side. Thereafter no cubes of that disease are placed during normal infections or Epidemics.
answers.evidence: Eradication: last cube of cured disease flips marker; uncured disease has no effect; eradicated diseases get no new cubes during infections or epidemics.

answers.answer: For a non-eradicated disease, an Epidemic places cubes to bring the named city to 3; with zero cubes, place 3. Reaching 3 does not itself cause an outbreak: the outbreak happens if the city already has cubes and the Epidemic would add cubes beyond the cap. Discard the Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile before Intensify reshuffles that pile and puts it on top of the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Infect step: place 3 cubes unless eradicated; if city already has cubes, add only enough to reach 3, then outbreak occurs; discard card. Outbreak rule is triggered at 3 when another cube would be placed.

answers.answer: Increase still occurs. The eradicated disease receives no cubes, but the Infection card is still discarded to the Infection Discard Pile and Intensify still reshuffles that pile onto the top of the Infection Deck. The Infect step still draws the bottom card.
answers.evidence: Epidemic steps occur in order; eradicated disease means no cubes placed; Infect step says discard the card; Intensify then reshuffles discard pile.

answers.answer: The first Epidemic's Intensify empties the Infection Discard Pile. The second bottom Infection card is then the only card shuffled by the second Intensify, and it ends on top. During the second Epidemic's Infect step, its named city starts at zero cubes and receives 3. When normal Infections immediately draws that city card, with no effects or protection, the city already has 3 cubes, so that Infection causes an outbreak instead of placing a fourth cube.
answers.evidence: Two Epidemics special rule: second bottom card is only card shuffled and ends on top; Epidemic Infect places 3 cubes in its named city; Infecting Cities: a city already at 3 triggers an outbreak.

answers.answer: The Scientist needs 4 City cards of the same color instead of 5 to Discover a Cure. The same requirements still apply: discard those cards at any research station, and the station city need not match the disease color.
answers.evidence: Cure Procedure and Scientist role; any research station works and station city's color need not match.

answers.answer: The Operations Expert builds a research station in the city they currently occupy as an action. No City card needs to be held, used, or discarded.
answers.evidence: Operations Expert: as an action, build a station in current city with no City card needed, used or discarded.

answers.answer: Once per turn, the Operations Expert may spend an action to move from a city with a research station to any city by discarding any City card. The summary does not specify whether this is in addition to, or replaces, a regular movement action; it states this as the role's special move. Dispatcher cannot use it when directing another pawn.
answers.evidence: Operations Expert: once per turn as an action, move from a research station to any city by discarding any City card; Dispatcher exception references this special move.

answers.answer: For an uncured disease, the Medic's Treat Disease action removes all cubes of one chosen color from the Medic's city. It can remove multiple cubes of that color, but does not remove cubes of other colors in that action.
answers.evidence: Medic: Treat Disease removes all cubes of one color; Treat Disease is color-specific and each different color takes a separate action.

answers.answer: When the cure is discovered, the Medic automatically removes all cubes of that cured color from any city the Medic occupies, without an action. Later, when moved into another city with cubes of that cured color by Dispatcher or Airlift, the Medic automatically removes all those cubes upon entering, also without an action; this works on another player's turn.
answers.evidence: Medic role: cured disease cubes automatically removed from any city entered or occupied, no action, including other players' turns if moved by Dispatcher or Airlift.

answers.answer: The Medic prevents placement and outbreaks of cured diseases in the Medic's own city. This does not protect adjacent cities or uncured diseases.
answers.evidence: Medic role: prevents placement and outbreaks of cured diseases in Medic's city, not adjacent cities or uncured diseases.

answers.answer: The Quarantine Specialist prevents placements and outbreaks of every disease color in the Specialist's current city and all connected cities. The ability does not affect cubes placed during setup.
answers.evidence: Quarantine Specialist role text.

answers.answer: Resilient Population removes any one card in the Infection Discard Pile from the game. It may be played between an Epidemic's Infect and Intensify steps, so it can remove the Infection card just discarded during that Epidemic before Intensify shuffles the remaining discard pile.
answers.evidence: Event table: remove any 1 card in Infection Discard Pile from game; may be played between Infect and Intensify steps.

answers.answer: One Quiet Night skips the next Infect Cities step, and no Infection cards are flipped for that skipped step. It does not skip an Epidemic's Infect step.
answers.evidence: Event table: skip next Infect Cities step, do not flip Infection cards; does not skip Epidemic Infect step.

answers.answer: Airlift moves any one pawn to any city. If it is another player's pawn, get that player's permission. Any player may play an Event at any time except between drawing and resolving a card; the player who plays it chooses how it is used.
answers.evidence: Airlift event effect; Event Cards timing and chooser rules.

answers.answer: Only Player cards count toward the 7-card hand limit. Role cards and Reference cards do not count, and the Contingency Planner's stored Event on the Role card also does not count. A hand of nine must be reduced by discarding cards or playing Event cards until it has at most seven.
answers.evidence: Hand Limit: Player cards only; Role and Reference cards do not count; discard or play Events until at most 7. Contingency Planner storage does not count against limit.

answers.answer: Government Grant places a research station in any city, with no requirement that the player be there and no City card discard required.
answers.evidence: Event table: Government Grant places a research station in any city, no card discard needed.

answers.answer: Forecast lets you draw, view, and rearrange the top 6 cards of the Infection Deck, then put them back on top of that deck.
answers.evidence: Event table: Forecast effect.
